items.text: Run timeout is 30 minutes (configurable per profile). Heartbeats fire every 15 seconds, with a 5-minute stale threshold. Token TTL should exceed run timeout — recommending TTL = run timeout + 5 min buffer (35 min default). No refresh needed: token is issued once at run start, expires after the run's configured timeout window. Revocation integrates with StopRun() / Terminator state transitions.

cli-core already has an HTTPClient (cliutil/httpclient.go) with Bearer token injection and a 30-second default timeout. The verification endpoint can reuse this client — scenarios call HTTPClient.Post('/api/v1/identity/verify', token) and get back verified claims. No new HTTP infrastructure needed.

Proposed token wire format: base64url(json_claims) + '.' + base64url(hmac_sha256(claims_bytes, server_secret)). Two segments separated by a dot, similar to a simplified JWT without the header segment. Claims JSON: {"run_id","task_id","profile_key","scope_path","iat","exp","meta":{}}. Total size: ~250-400 bytes base64-encoded, well within env var limits.

The injection point is confirmed: RunExecutor.SandboxEnvVars() (run_executor.go:923-941) returns map[string]string merged into ExecuteRequest.Environment, which flows through buildEnv() → cmd.Env. A new IdentityEnvVars() method on RunExecutor would follow the same pattern. Both sandbox and identity vars get injected for all run modes (identity is orthogonal to sandbox).

Swarm-manager uses unverified string fields: execution.Record.StartedBy, PromptSkillVersion.CreatedBy. These are populated at request time with no verification. Once the identity standard ships, swarm-manager can verify the VROOLI_AGENT_IDENTITY_TOKEN against agent-manager before trusting attribution — the downstream execute item (swarm-manager-identity-adoption) already exists for this work.

items.context: Default run timeout is 30 min (configurable per profile). Heartbeats fire every 15s with 5-min stale threshold. Options for how token TTL relates to run lifetime.

options.label: Static TTL = run timeout + 5 min buffer
options.rationale: Simple. Token issued at run start with TTL matching the run's configured timeout plus a small buffer for post-run result collection. No refresh mechanism needed. Revocation on run cancellation/failure invalidates early. Default: 35 min.

options.label: Short TTL (5 min) with heartbeat-based refresh
options.rationale: Tighter security window — tokens expire fast if not refreshed. But adds complexity: agents need a refresh endpoint, and cli-core needs retry-on-401 logic. Heartbeat interval (15s) provides natural refresh cadence.

options.label: No expiry — revocation only
options.rationale: Token valid until explicitly revoked by run completion/cancellation. Simplest implementation but tokens remain valid indefinitely if revocation fails.

items.freeform: Option A but the timeout should be a day. Agents are getting more capable over time as AI improves, which includes the amount of time they can run. 30 minutes is already short, and they’ll likely be able to run for hours pretty soon. So 1 day is a better default

items.context: The REST verification endpoint (POST /api/v1/identity/verify) needs a defined request/response contract. The endpoint validates the HMAC signature and checks expiry/revocation, returning the verified claims on success.

options.label: Single verify endpoint that returns full claims
options.rationale: POST /api/v1/identity/verify with {"token": "..."} body. Returns 200 with full claims JSON on success, 401 on invalid/expired/revoked. Simple and sufficient — consumers get everything in one call.

options.label: Verify endpoint + separate introspection endpoint
options.rationale: POST /api/v1/identity/verify for scenario-side verification. GET /api/v1/identity/me for agents to introspect their own identity without parsing the token. Two endpoints but clearer separation of concerns.

items.context: When a scenario can't reach agent-manager to verify a token (network issue, agent-manager restarting), it needs a fallback strategy. This affects how strictly consumers should enforce identity verification.

options.label: Fail open with warning — fall back to anonymous attribution
options.rationale: If verification fails due to network issues, treat the request as anonymous/unverified and log a warning. Matches the backward-compat model where missing tokens = anonymous. Avoids blocking work due to transient infra issues.

options.label: Fail closed — reject unverifiable requests
options.rationale: If token can't be verified, reject the request. Stronger security but risks blocking legitimate work during agent-manager restarts or network blips.

options.label: Cache-based fallback — cache verified claims with short TTL
options.rationale: After first successful verification, cache the claims for 2-5 minutes. If agent-manager is unreachable, use cached result. Balances security with availability but adds caching complexity to cli-core.

plan_updates: Incorporated round 1 decisions (HMAC-SHA256, server-side verify, REST, minimal+metadata claims). Added findings on token lifecycle, wire format, injection point, cli-core HTTP client reuse, and swarm-manager attribution patterns. Updated conclusion with detailed token format, verification endpoint contract, lifecycle design, consumer interface, and env var convention.
